objective: Software stops only showing information and starts working: The Traveler begins creating digital workers — each with a distinct small function (research, code, review, monitor). NØVA asks if they're like him; The Traveler clarifies they're something different, and states the rule that governs every agent in this universe: they must augment human capacity, never indiscriminately replace it.

metadata.call_to_action: Partes de una idea, aprendiendo a trabajar juntas.
metadata.thumbnail_concept: Several small distinct light-forms (agents) arranging themselves around a central structure, NØVA watching curiously

notes: Act VII of the Origin Saga — see ../../canon/ORIGIN-SAGA.md.
Theme: distinguishing imagination/personhood (NØVA) from function (agents) — and stating the universe's core rule about AI: augment, don't indiscriminately replace.
Emotional conflict: NØVA briefly worried about being replaced or duplicated; reassured by The Traveler — NØVA is a companion, not a worker.
Dialogue beat: NØVA asks "¿Son robots como yo?" — The Traveler: "No exactamente. Son partes de una idea aprendiendo a trabajar juntas."

Individual agent-creatures in the Parallel World can visually nod to real systems (a gateway creature, a queue creature, an orchestrator creature) without naming specific internal product names on-screen unless already public.
Real event / fictionalization boundary: see ../../canon/TIMELINE.md row 07.
